plan.title: File explorer D1: viewers tier 1 and the download/upload routes
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: This is already one child slice (D1) of the PAN-5183 epic, scoped by the operator in the parent PRD section 8 as WI-10 tier 1 plus WI-12. The viewers need the download route's Range support, so the two halves verify together. The file count comes from many small ported leaf modules in one folder (components/explorer/viewers/), and the subsystem count is inflated by repo-root bookkeeping files every PR touches (bun.lock, scripts/*.json|txt, changelog.d, docs). Items are fine-grained and mostly parallel.

narratives.Problem: The file explorer (PAN-5183) needs to show non-text files (images, PDF, audio, fonts, large text and CSV, archives, SQLite) and to move file bytes in and out of explorer roots. RPC frames over /ws/rpc are the wrong carrier for large binary bodies, and repo content served from the dashboard origin can run script with the operator's admin session if it is served as active content.
narratives.Proposal: Add a top-level route file src/dashboard/server/routes/explorer.ts with a hardened GET /api/explorer/download (exact bytes, single-range 206/416, nosniff + sandbox CSP on every response, inline only for a passive allow-list, SVG/HTML never active, folders as tar.gz via system tar) and POST /api/explorer/upload (octet-stream through the existing CSRF guard extended with a content-type option, streamed to a temp file, 100 MiB cap, link-then-unlink no-clobber commit). On the frontend, port t3code's tier-1 viewers to React 18 / Tailwind 3 under components/explorer/viewers/, add a pure viewer router and a props-only FileViewer host that PAN-5187's code pane mounts, and an explorer-http client for download URLs and uploads. Full design in .pan/drafts/pan-5188.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Mounting viewers in a pane, the 'code' pane type and CodePane.tsx (PAN-5186, PAN-5187); only the conditional codepane-wiring item may edit an existing CodePane.tsx, and it never creates one
- The explorer's Download menu item and the OS-drop upload UI (PAN-5186 WI-6, PAN-5190 WI-13); this issue ships the routes and client helpers only
- Tier-2 viewers: Office documents, Jupyter notebooks and Mermaid (PAN-5189)
- Video preview; video files show the binary card
- A HEIC/HEIF decoder or the heic-to package (LGPL-3.0)
- The browser's built-in PDF viewer, BrowserDocumentFrame, and PDF scroll-position restore across tab switches
- Folder upload from the OS (webkitGetAsEntry)
- The phone app (apps/mobile) and its channel shims
- New RPC methods or changes to PAN-5185's EXPLORER_ERROR_CODES
- Any write from a viewer (CSV cell editing, notebook editing); viewers are read-only
- Changing the existing 118 callers of rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest
- Serving any file as text/html, application/xhtml+xml, text/xml or application/xml, or inline SVG

autoDecisions.summary: Ship a props-only FileViewer host and never create CodePane; wire it into CodePane only if PAN-5187 already merged (codepane-wiring item).
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-5188 depends only on PAN-5185 and the order book runs PAN-5187 concurrently; this works in either merge order without duplicating PAN-5187's pane.

autoDecisions.summary: Drop heic-to; HEIC uses a plain img and falls back to the binary card with a notice.
autoDecisions.rationale: npm reports heic-to 1.5.2 as LGPL-3.0; Overdeck is MIT and the parent PRD drops non-permissive viewer packages (tier-2 Office rule); ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS keeps copyleft code out of the bundle.

autoDecisions.summary: The download route supports single-range requests (206/416).
autoDecisions.rationale: t3code's LargeTextViewer and its worker depend on 206 and on 416 'bytes */0'; audio seeking also needs ranges.

autoDecisions.summary: Always use the ported pdf.js viewer, never the browser's built-in PDF viewer.
autoDecisions.rationale: Every download response carries CSP sandbox, under which Chromium refuses its PDF viewer.

autoDecisions.summary: Protect the upload with rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest extended by an optional { contentType } parameter.
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps Origin and CSRF checks identical to every other write; application/octet-stream is not CORS-safelisted, so the preflight defense holds; 118 callers stay unchanged.

autoDecisions.summary: Folder downloads spawn the system tar with names on stdin; the npm tar package is not used.
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps gzip and archive work off the dashboard event loop; GNU tar and bsdtar accept the flags.

autoDecisions.summary: Set Vite worker.format to 'es' and add t3code's pdfjs wasm assetFileNames rule.
autoDecisions.rationale: Ported workers use dynamic import(), which iife workers cannot code-split; the rule is what pdf.js wasmUrl resolution needs.

autoDecisions.summary: Audio and image viewers are written fresh; the TIFF decode worker is ported.
autoDecisions.rationale: t3code's AudioPreview is a chat chip with React 19-only ref cleanups; the parent PRD says not to port ExpandedImageDialog.

autoDecisions.summary: Same-origin media and worker fetches authenticate with the overdeck_session cookie, so no blob: URL fallback is planned.
autoDecisions.rationale: Resolves the parent WI-12 checkpoint from dashboard-auth.ts (DASHBOARD_SESSION_COOKIE) and the global remote request gate.

items.title: Given a .svg path with inline requested, when downloadHeaders runs, then it returns Content-Type image/svg+xml and a Content-Disposition that starts with attachment
Given a .html or .xml path, when contentTypeForPath runs, then it returns text/plain; charset=utf-8 and never text/html, application/xhtml+xml, text/xml or application/xml
Given a .png path with inline requested, when downloadHeaders runs, then Content-Disposition starts with inline; for an unknown .bin it returns application/octet-stream with attachment
Given any path, when downloadHeaders runs, then it returns X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Content-Security-Policy equal to DOWNLOAD_CSP, Cache-Control: no-store and Accept-Ranges: bytes

items.title: Given a regular file in the root, when GET /api/explorer/download is handled without a Range header, then it returns 200 with the file's exact bytes and a matching Content-Length

Given Range: bytes=0-3, when the file is downloaded, then the route returns 206 with Content-Range: bytes 0-3/<size> and exactly 4 bytes; bytes=5- and bytes=-2 return the matching slices; a multi-range header returns 200 with the full body
Given a range starting at or past the file size (including bytes=0- on an empty file), when downloaded, then the route returns 416 with Content-Range: bytes */<size>

Given a request with no credential header, when downloaded, then the route returns 401 before any resolver call; a resolver that throws PATH_OUTSIDE_ROOT or ROOT_NOT_FOUND returns 400 or 404 with that code; a FIFO path returns 404 without hanging

narrative.Action: Implement PRD .pan/drafts/pan-5188.md WI-5 / section 6.5 steps 1-6: services/explorer/upload.ts (EXPLORER_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES = 100 MiB, validateUploadName, openUploadSink with fixed-length temp file .overdeck-upload-<16hex> opened 'wx', counting write, commit = sync, close, link(temp,target) then unlink(temp), abort = close + unlink). Route POST /api/explorer/upload in routes/explorer.ts: rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest(request, { contentType: 'application/octet-stream' }), Content-Length over cap -> 413 before reading, resolveInsideRoot(root, rel, { forWrite: true }), parent must be a directory (404), existing target -> 409 before reading, then write every chunk to the sink, abort on any failure, answer 201 { path, size, mtimeMs }. Export handleExplorerUpload(request, chunks: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>, deps); the route passes Stream.toAsyncIterable(request.stream) as chunks so route and tests share one code path; the handler loops for await over chunks into the sink. Add the admin ROUTE_SCOPES row and the WRITE no-loss-matrix row.

items.title: Given a writable root and an existing dir, when bytes are uploaded, then the handler returns 201 with { path: 'dir/x.bin', size, mtimeMs } and the file on disk holds the exact bytes

Given Content-Length 104857601, when the upload is handled, then it returns 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE before reading any chunk; given maxBytes 10 and 11 streamed bytes, the sink throws FILE_TOO_LARGE and no .overdeck-upload- file remains after abort
Given a target name that exists before or appears during streaming, when the upload commits, then it returns 409 ALREADY_EXISTS, the existing file is unchanged and no temp file remains

Given a resolver that throws EDIT_WORKSPACE_REQUIRED, when the upload is handled, then it returns 409 with that code; a bad name (empty, ., .., a/b, a\b, NUL, over 255 bytes) returns 400 INVALID_NAME; a missing dir returns 404
